DynamicExploit.description:
DAST / dynamic-reproduction block for a confirmed finding -- how to reproduce the exploit
against a RUNNING target, authored PURELY by the exploit-writer LLM (no deterministic
construction). It complements the runnable script in :class:`ProofOfConcept.payload` with
operator-facing reproduction, and is MODALITY-CORRECT for the finding's language + vuln class:

  * ``vector == "http"`` -- a web-reachable sink: use ``http_method`` + ``url`` (FICTIONAL host,
    accurate route path) + ``path`` + ``param``.
  * ``vector in {"cli-arg","stdin","env","file","ipc","function-call"}`` -- a LOCAL / native
    target (C/C++ memory-safety, a CLI tool, a library call): there is NO URL. Use ``command``
    (build + run the binary/program with the crafted input) and the input channel. NEVER invent a
    fictional URL for a target that is not network-reachable.

Common to both: ``payload`` (concrete attack input), ``steps`` (numbered reproduction), and
``expected_response`` (observable proof: HTTP status/body OR crash/segfault/overwrite/command exec).

Descriptive ENRICHMENT only -- it never gates detection and carries no precision/FP claim. Present
only when a validated PoC was attached.

command.description: Local reproduction command: build + run the target with the crafted input, e.g. `gcc vuln.c -o vuln && ./vuln "$(python3 -c 'print("A"*512)')"`. Empty for pure-http findings.
command.title: Command

dynamic_mode.description: Recommended live-reproduction modality for the dynamic exploit agent: 'playwright' when the attacker input is entered through the VISIBLE UI (form field, search box, link); 'mitm' when it rides a REQUEST NOT EXPOSED IN THE UI (hidden/JSON POST field, API param, tampered header/cookie) needing interception; 'python' when it is HARD TO PLACE via http/browser (native/CLI vector, multi-step scripted or binary/protocol attack -> run the PoC). Empty if unsure (agent decides).
dynamic_mode.title: Dynamic Mode

dynamic_mode_reason.description: One short clause on WHY that modality (e.g. 'input is a visible search field', 'param only sent in a background JSON POST', 'stack overflow via CLI arg').
dynamic_mode_reason.title: Dynamic Mode Reason

expected_response.description: Observable proof: HTTP status/body marker, OR crash/segfault/memory-overwrite/command execution.
expected_response.title: Expected Response

http_method.description: HTTP verb (GET|POST|...) when vector==http; else empty.
http_method.title: Http Method

payload.description: The concrete attack payload/input delivered (no placeholders).
payload.title: Payload

steps.description: Ordered, human-followable steps to reproduce dynamically.
steps.title: Steps

url.description: FICTIONAL target URL incl. accurate route path (vector==http only), e.g. http://target.example/search?q=PAYLOAD
url.title: Url

vector.description: Delivery channel: http | cli-arg | stdin | env | file | ipc | function-call.
vector.title: Vector

DynamicExploit.title: DynamicExploit

Evidence.description:
One piece of corroboration (or refutation) for a finding.

The pipeline accumulates these as it runs. A finding is 'grounded' when
it has at least one ``check == 'pass'`` Evidence whose ``kind`` is
``file_exists`` *and* one whose ``kind`` is ``snippet_match`` (or
equivalent ground-truth signal). Findings without grounding evidence
get their severity capped at ``MEDIUM`` and tagged ``weak-evidence``.

kind.description: file_exists | line_resolves | snippet_match | structural_hit | poc_runnable | reachable
kind.title: Kind

Evidence.title: Evidence

Finding.description:
A single triage candidate produced by the pipeline.

Findings are immutable once emitted — stages that ``refine`` a finding
construct a new one with the same ``id`` and a bumped revision count.

abstained.description: True iff the finding fell in the calibrated abstention band and is routed to a human as 'uncertain'.
abstained.title: Abstained

attack_chain.description: Ordered narrative of how an attacker reaches the sink.
attack_chain.title: Attack Chain

calibrated_confidence.description: Platt-calibrated probability from reviewer history (improvement #8). None = not calibrated.
calibrated_confidence.title: Calibrated Confidence

corroborating_tools.description: Names of external scanners that independently flagged this finding.
corroborating_tools.title: Corroborating Tools

cvss_score_original.description: The CVSS score before this finding was demoted, when it was. A demotion for a CONFIDENCE reason used to change the label and leave the score alone, so the record said `low` and `9.1` at once and a consumer believed whichever field it read first. The score now moves with the label and the original is kept here rather than lost.
cvss_score_original.title: Cvss Score Original

evidence.description: Pass/fail records produced by the grounding pass and other checks.
evidence.title: Evidence

externally_corroborated.description: True iff an independent scanner (Semgrep/CodeQL/Bandit/Trivy) also flagged this file:line:cwe (improvement #2).
externally_corroborated.title: Externally Corroborated

grounded.description: True iff S4b grounding pass verified file + line + snippet.
grounded.title: Grounded

impact.description: Coarse impact family derived deterministically from the CWE (the 'sink signal'): rce | sqli | nosqli | traversal | ssrf | xss | open-redirect | xxe | ldapi | xpathi | crypto | disclosure | access-control | trust-boundary | other. Pairs with taint.source_origin for an (attack-surface x impact) risk lens. Descriptive only.
impact.title: Impact

poc_confidence.description: CWE-class-aware PoC confidence/modality (#134). Present on every confirmed TP the exploit stage sees -- even evidence-only classes where no payload PoC is written.

poc_demonstrated.description: True iff the behavioral PoC oracle proved the payload subverts the sink (improvement #6).
poc_demonstrated.title: Poc Demonstrated

provenance.description: Reproducibility trail: model, prompt_sha256, seed/temperature, structural_index_sha (improvement #10).
provenance.title: Provenance

reachability.description: 0..1 -- can an external entrypoint reach this sink? (None = not computed)
reachability.title: Reachability

Finding.title: Finding

Location.description: A single file:line[:end_line] reference attached to a finding.

snippet.description: ?25 lines of context for human reviewers.
snippet.title: Snippet

Location.title: Location

PoCConfidence.description:
How confident/exploitable the exploit agent's PoC is, given the CWE class (#134).

A verified true positive does not imply an equally writable PoC: this records the PoC MODALITY
(payload / path / sequence / evidence_only) and a ceiling-capped confidence, so PoCs can be
filtered/drilled-down. ``modality == 'evidence_only'`` (crypto/config) means no payload exploit
exists -- the finding is still a true positive, just reported with evidence rather than a PoC.

poc_attempted.description: False when the exploit agent skipped payload generation (evidence-only class).
poc_attempted.title: Poc Attempted

PoCConfidence.title: PoCConfidence

ProofOfConcept.description:
Concrete demonstration that the finding is exploitable.

A real PoC is a string the operator could paste into curl, a file, or
a request body. A *generic* PoC ("send a malicious value") is treated
as no PoC at all -- this is enforced by :meth:`Finding.has_concrete_poc`.

dynamic.description: DAST / dynamic-reproduction block (steps-to-reproduce + HTTP shape + fictional URL + concrete payload) authored by the exploit-writer LLM alongside the script.

invocation.description: How to deliver the payload (curl line, function call, etc.).
invocation.title: Invocation

is_concrete.description: True only if payload + invocation contain non-placeholder content.
is_concrete.title: Is Concrete

language.description: Exploit script language when `payload` is a full script, e.g. 'python'.
language.title: Language

ProofOfConcept.title: ProofOfConcept

Severity.description:
SARIF-aligned severity ordering.

The string values match the SARIF ``level`` vocabulary so the SARIF
emitter can pass them through verbatim.
Severity.title: Severity

StageResult.description: The output of one pipeline stage.

finished_at.description: Absolute UTC timestamp when this stage finished.
finished_at.title: Finished At

started_at.description: Absolute UTC timestamp when this stage began.
started_at.title: Started At

StageResult.title: StageResult

TaintFlow.description:
The shape every research-lens finding must fill in.

A vulnerability without a *source*, a *sink*, and a path between them is
a vibe, not a finding. Forcing the lens to declare these three slots
explicitly is the single biggest hallucination reducer in this harness:
if the model can't name them, it shouldn't be writing the finding.

attack_vector.description: Derived from source_origin: 'remote' (network) or 'local' (cli-arg/env/file/ipc). Lets a reviewer tell a remotely-reachable flow from a local-only one (e.g. getenv->exec).
attack_vector.title: Attack Vector

proof_basis.description: Deterministic proof summary carried from the Tier-1 taint engine (source→hops→sink + sanitizer status), so Tier-2 / exploit / patch stages verify against the proven path instead of re-inferring it. Descriptive only — never gates.
proof_basis.title: Proof Basis

sanitizer_missing.description: True if the lens claims no sanitizer is present on the path.
sanitizer_missing.title: Sanitizer Missing

sanitizers_observed.description: Sanitizers the lens *did* see on the path (helps disprove FPs).
sanitizers_observed.title: Sanitizers Observed

source_origin.description: Attack surface the tainted data enters from: 'network' (HTTP/socket -- remote) | 'cli-arg' | 'env' | 'file' | 'ipc' (all local). Deterministic; descriptive only.
source_origin.title: Source Origin

taint_path.description: Ordered list of locations the data flows through, source to sink.
taint_path.title: Taint Path

TaintFlow.title: TaintFlow

VerificationResult.description:
Final outcome-verification verdict for a finding (stage S8c).

Collapses the independent signals earlier stages already gathered
(grounding, taint completeness, concrete PoC, reachability, voter
agreement) into a single auditable verdict. Deterministic by default,
so it works identically on every backend -- including ones that reject
``temperature`` (Opus / cli) where multi-agent voting is a no-op.

agreement.description: Fraction of self-consistency samples that confirmed.
agreement.title: Agreement

signals.description: Per-signal pass/fail (grounded, taint_complete, concrete_poc, reachable, vote_confirmed).
signals.title: Signals

threshold.description: K independent signals required for verified=True.
threshold.title: Threshold

VerificationResult.title: VerificationResult

Vote.description: One model's vote on a candidate finding (used during S6 voting).

role.description: Logical role name from the profile.
role.title: Role

Vote.title: Vote

description: Audit record written next to every scan output.

backend_degraded.description: True if a network LLM backend failed mid-run and could not be used (W0.1/C1). In a real scan the failing stage raises and is recorded as an error rather than silently falling back to the mock backend, so Tier-2 output is PARTIAL. Confident-tier FP=0 is unaffected (the deterministic tier does not use an LLM). Under tests/CI the mock fallback still runs but the degradation is flagged here.
backend_degraded.title: Backend Degraded

budget_exceeded.description: True if the run hit the global budget and skipped remaining paid stages.
budget_exceeded.title: Budget Exceeded

coverage.description: File-parser scan coverage: source_files_parsed, coverage_pct, complete (True iff no recognized source file was dropped by a limit), by_language, and per-reason skip counts. Surfaced for the UI.
coverage.title: Coverage

file_hashes.description: Per-file content hashes (relative path -> sha256) for the scanned scope. Used by --incremental to skip unchanged files next run.
file_hashes.title: File Hashes

hallucination_metrics.description: Counters surfaced by the grounding and PoC stages. Keys: raw_lens, ungrounded_dropped, ungrounded_downgraded, missing_poc, missing_taint, validator_rejected, voted_out.
hallucination_metrics.title: Hallucination Metrics

llm_usage.description: Per-scan LLM usage across ALL backends (local + cloud): requests, tokens_in/out/total, cost_usd, and a by_provider breakdown (each with by_model). Captured at the backend choke point so it is provider-agnostic. Persisted to the DB with the manifest.
llm_usage.title: Llm Usage

max_wall_seconds.description: Global per-run wall-clock ceiling in seconds (0 = unlimited).
max_wall_seconds.title: Max Wall Seconds

run_config.description: Effective, resolved configuration for this run: models per role (backend/model/temperature/max_tokens/timeout) and the precision-gate posture (voting quorum/voters, s4b/s8b/s8c strict, s8c threshold, seeding). Surfaced so the UI/audit shows exactly how the scan was run.
run_config.title: Run Config

scan_id.description: The scan's UUID -- the key every scan_id-segmented store uses. Set from `application_id`, which has carried the globally-unique run id since #254. Optional because manifests from OLDER builds carry none; a reader must then fall back to `application_id` rather than mint a replacement, since a fresh UUID matches nothing.
scan_id.title: Scan Id

src_bytes.description: Total bytes of source scanned (sum over parsed source files).
src_bytes.title: Src Bytes

src_loc.description: Total source lines of code scanned (sum over parsed source files).
src_loc.title: Src Loc

time_exceeded.description: True if the run hit the wall-clock deadline and stopped launching new paid work. Findings are partial; confident-tier FP=0 is preserved (only deterministically-grounded findings are emitted).
time_exceeded.title: Time Exceeded

total_seconds.description: True end-to-end scan wall-clock duration (monotonic), i.e. real elapsed time from scan start to finish -- NOT the sum of per-stage durations.
total_seconds.title: Total Seconds
